The mutation onSuccess (which shows the toast, closes the dialog, resets multiEmailValue) does not reset isInvalidEmail, and no effect resets it on dialog open/close. So a stale validation banner can persist into the next dialog session, as described. It's a minor UX defect but a real, verifiable incorrect behavior introduced by this diff.

judged_text: isInvalidEmail is never reset on mutation success or dialog close (only the cancel button resets it), so the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner persists into the next dialog session. A user who once submitted invalid input, then closes via success or the X/overlay, reopens the dialog for another booking and sees a validation error banner before typing anything — misdirecting them into thinking their fresh input is invalid.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd`), but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. On mutation success, the code closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail` (`onSuccess` only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false); setMultiEmailValue([""]);`). Also, closing the dialog via `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` (overlay/X) does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Since the dialog component stays mounted in `BookingListItem` and only toggles `open`, the stale error banner can persist into the next open session.
